answer: Because the voyage fee is applied at the ferrous exit, the cipher audit totals the burn and the ledger shows exactly what left. Withdrawing stake costs a 15% fee that is burned rather than redistributed, so moving capital between aliases destroys a slice of it every time. An operator rotating funds across many keys thus bleeds value on each hop, which is a cost an agent that leaves its stake in place never forfeits. That is 31 dollars per alias. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
